title: Map personal choice and context in one ordinary route

sections.title: Understand the distinction
sections.body: A route combines personal choices with transport, cost, language, access and rules. A thought experiment can expose a dependency without claiming another group’s lived experience.

sections.title: Complete fictional practice material
sections.body: Complete fictional library route: bus leaves home stop 09:00, arrives 09:20; suitable step-free entrance is 5 minutes away; library opens 09:30. Return bus leaves 10:30, arrives home 10:50. Fare 2 units each way; Jo has 5 discretionary units and needs to be home 11:00. A public notice says the borrowed book can be returned at the staffed desk; online renewal is unavailable for this item. No alternative transport is confirmed.

sections.title: Work through the supplied case
sections.body: Trace time, cost, access and the rule. Then change one fact: the 09:00 bus is cancelled. Identify what can be chosen and what needs new information.

sections.title: Try a different case before checking
sections.body: A form is free but only available in an unreadable format for its user. Does zero price establish equal access?

checks.title: Compare reasoning and review the supplied result
checks.body: Original route reaches the entrance 09:25, waits 5 minutes, costs 4 with 1 remaining, and arrives home 10 minutes before the duty. Cancellation removes the known outward route; another bus or helper must be verified, not invented. Partial: know the library hours but omit travel. Incorrect: blame lack of determination or assume stairs are a suitable substitute.
criteria: The complete route uses supplied dependencies
Structural constraint is not recast as personal fault

checks.title: Check the changed case
checks.body: No. Format, language, support and an accepted submission route still matter. Record the barrier and seek an actual suitable alternative rather than claiming universal exclusion or universal accessibility from price alone.
